title: The Psychology of Technology in Film Making with Andy Philpo

sentences.en: How do I act so well?
sentences.zh: 我是怎么演得那么好的？

sentences.en: What I do is I pretend to be the person I'm portraying in the film or play.
sentences.zh: 我所做的就是假装自己是电影或戏剧中我所扮演的那个人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You're confused.
sentences.zh: 你感到困惑了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: It's perfectly simple.
sentences.zh: 这非常简单。

sentences.en: Case in point, Lord of the Rings.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，《指环王》。

sentences.en: Peter Jackson comes from New Zealand and says to me,
sentences.zh: 彼得·杰克逊从新西兰过来对我说：

sentences.en: Sir Ian, I want you to be Gandalf the Wizard.
sentences.zh: 伊恩爵士，我想让你扮演巫师甘道夫。

sentences.en: And I say to him, you are aware that I am not really a wizard.
sentences.zh: 我对他说，你知道我并不是真的巫师吧。

sentences.en: And he said, yes, I am aware of that.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，我知道。

sentences.en: What I want you to do is to use your acting skills to portray the wizard for the duration of the film.
sentences.zh: 我想要你做的是运用你的演技，在电影拍摄期间扮演好这个巫师。

sentences.en: So I said, okay.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，好吧。

sentences.en: And then I said to myself, hmm, how would I do that?
sentences.zh: 然后我对自己说，嗯，我该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: And this is what I did.
sentences.zh: 于是我这样做。

sentences.en: I imagined what it would be like to be a wizard.
sentences.zh: 我想象了一下成为巫师会是什么样子。

sentences.en: And then I pretended and acted in that way on the day.
sentences.zh: 然后在拍摄当天，我就假装并以那种方式表演。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And how did I know what to say?
sentences.zh: 那我怎么知道该说什么呢？

sentences.en: The words were written down for me in a script.

sentences.en: How did I know where to stand?

sentences.en: People told me.

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.zh: 但当你是一个站在舞台上的单口喜剧演员，对着观众大喊“别笑了”时。

sentences.en: So, we've talked a little bit about filmmaking before.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们之前聊过一点电影制作。

sentences.en: You know, you're more kind of on the technical end of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你更多是在技术层面。

sentences.en: And I was hoping that this would kind of turn into like a filmmaking series.
sentences.zh: 我本来希望这能变成一个电影制作系列。

sentences.en: We had a couple guests, Chris Rogers, who wrote Halt and Catch Fire and Paper Girls.
sentences.zh: 我们请过几位嘉宾，比如写过《奔腾年代》和《纸女孩》的克里斯·罗杰斯。

sentences.en: And a couple shows that I like is going to come on.
sentences.zh: 还有几部我喜欢的剧的主创也要来。

sentences.en: We'll record that next week.
sentences.zh: 我们下周会录制。

sentences.en: I don't know when it'll go out.
sentences.zh: 我不知道什么时候会播出。

sentences.en: And I don't want to, like, say who they are because people definitely have the right to, like, not come on a show like this, which is probably a waste of their time.
sentences.zh: 我不想说他们是谁，因为人们绝对有权利选择不来参加这样的节目，这可能是在浪费他们的时间。

sentences.en: You know, but they sent a couple of different emails to people that are trying to see if we can make it work with scheduling and whatever of, like, little things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但我们给不同的人发了几封邮件，试图看看能否协调好日程安排之类的小事。

sentences.en: So, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道。

sentences.en: Maybe we'll get a critical mass of some Hollywood people.
sentences.zh: 也许我们能凑齐一批好莱坞人士。

sentences.en: But I thought it'd be fun to talk about the way that you're applying technology because it is so different.
sentences.zh: 但我认为聊聊你应用技术的方式会很有趣，因为它太不一样了。

sentences.en: And even though some of the things, like, you had talked a little bit about Disney's projects, but even though, like, what you're doing is, like, way more state of the art,
sentences.zh: 尽管你之前聊过一些迪士尼的项目，但即使你现在做的这些比90年代的蓝幕技术先进得多，

sentences.en: I guess, than even, you know, the blue screen 90s stuff, it feels older world.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，它反而有一种旧时代的感觉。

sentences.en: Like, it feels like the soundstage, you know, 70s type filmmaking that I like more than whatever we've done for the past 15 years.
sentences.zh: 就像我更喜欢的70年代那种摄影棚电影制作，而不是过去15年我们所做的那样。

sentences.en: So, the psychology of that, I think, is ripe for discussion.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这背后的心理学很值得讨论。

sentences.en: And I'll turn that over to you.
sentences.zh: 现在交给你了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I no longer work at Disney.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我不在迪士尼工作了。

sentences.en: I've moved on to some other things.
sentences.zh: 我已经转向其他领域了。

sentences.en: But, of course, they're the big touchstone for, like, visual effects and production and things like that.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他们仍然是视觉特效、制作等方面的标杆。

sentences.en: So, now I do a lot of, like, concert design, live events, things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我做了很多演唱会设计、现场活动之类的工作。

sentences.en: But the technology that you're talking about, sort of what gets labeled in the industry as, like, in-camera VFX, right?
sentences.zh: 但你提到的那种技术，也就是行业内所谓的“机内特效”，对吧？

sentences.en: Now is, you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: It's, like, a super old technology because the oldest versions of it was, like, you hung up a big rear projection screen behind the, like, James Bond car.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一种超级古老的技术，因为最早的版本就是你在詹姆斯·邦德的汽车后面挂一个巨大的背投屏幕。

sentences.en: And then you rolled your, like, B-roll of the California, like, countryside behind it.
sentences.zh: 然后你在后面播放加州乡村的B卷素材。

sentences.en: And, like, that was how you got the effect of someone driving.
sentences.zh: 这就是你获得驾驶效果的方式。

sentences.en: And so, there's been a confluence of technologies in the last, say, 10 years, maybe, that have made it possible to kind of, like,
sentences.zh: 所以，过去十年左右，多种技术的融合使得这种机内特效能够回归到现代制作模式中。

sentences.en: bring that sort of in-camera effect back to modern production paradigMs.
sentences.zh: 这非常具体，而且考虑到它与其他技术进步的关系，这很有趣。

sentences.en: And they are very specifically, and it's interesting because of the relationship to the other, like, advancements in technology we've seen.
sentences.zh: 但第一项技术就是低像素间距的LED面板，对吧？

sentences.en: But the first one is very, like, low pixel pitch LED tile, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以拥有很多这样的面板，就像你的电视分辨率超高一样。

sentences.en: So, you can have lots of that, like, your TV is, like, super high res.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把它做成墙壁大小，对吧？

sentences.en: We can make that at, like, a wall-sized scale, right?
sentences.zh: 每个人都看过关于《曼达洛人》使用巨大LED墙的纪录片。

sentences.en: Like, everyone's seen the documentary about the Mandalorian with the big LED wall.
sentences.zh: 我不确定每个人都看过。

sentences.en: I don't know that everyone has.
sentences.zh: 如果你不介意的话，能给我们讲讲那种技术在片场是什么样子的吗？

sentences.en: If you don't mind, like, telling us a little bit about what that technology looks like on a set.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得电影极客们对此有敌意，很多人一听到技术就说“别把那玩意儿放进我的电影里”。

sentences.en: Because I think the hostility from film nerds, a lot of people hear technology and they say, like, get that out of my movie.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不想要《星球大战》第一部那种感觉。

sentences.en: Like, I don't want, you know, episode one of Star Wars.
sentences.zh: 我想要原版三部曲之类的。

sentences.en: I want the original trilogy or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们想到的是人们在绿幕前跑来跑去，没有任何参考点。

sentences.en: And they think of people running around green screen where there's no reference point.
sentences.zh: 你知道，基本上是成千上万的工程师在制作电影，而不是电影制作人。

sentences.en: And, you know, basically thousands of engineers making a movie instead of a filmmaker.
sentences.zh: 但我们回归的方式更像是旧世界，老派好莱坞。

sentences.en: But what we've gone back to is a little bit more like the old world, old Hollywood.
sentences.zh: 是的，那种技术，就是大家在提到扩展现实场景和机内特效时想到的标杆。

sentences.en: Yeah, so what that technology is, the touchstone that everyone thinks about with, like, extended reality sets in camera VFX.
sentences.zh: 这些是人们使用的流行词。

sentences.en: These are, like, the buzzwords that people use for it.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，它就是一面巨大的LED墙，就像你在演唱会上看到的那样。

sentences.en: But essentially what it is, it's a huge LED wall, like you would see at, like, a concert.
sentences.zh: 它是弯曲的吗？

sentences.en: Does it curve?
sentences.zh: 就像圆顶，或者IMAX那种？

sentences.en: Like, is it like a dome, like an IMAX thing?
sentences.zh: 它可以是平的，但《曼达洛人》专门使用的是弯曲的LED表面。

sentences.en: It can be flat, but the one specifically from Mandalorian is a curved LED surface.
sentences.zh: 然后他们在头顶上放几块面板来做一个类似天花板的东西。

sentences.en: And then they do, like, a handful of tiles overhead to make, like, kind of a ceiling.
sentences.zh: 但那些通常只是平坦的平面，用来捕捉一些天空的效果。

sentences.en: But those are typically just a flat plane that's kind of just capturing some of the sky effect.
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 但你仍然能获得环境光，这改变了摄像机捕捉光线的方式，你知道，光线从演员身上反射出来，所有那些……

sentences.en: But you're still getting the ambient lighting that changes the way that the camera, you know, light bounces off the actors and all that stuff that...
sentences.zh: 对，那是……

sentences.en: Right, and that's...
sentences.zh: 让一切看起来很真实。

sentences.en: Makes it look like they're real.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以……

sentences.en: Yeah, so...
sentences.zh: 那才是最大的区别，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's really the big difference, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是它优于绿幕的地方，你知道，你在绿幕片场看到某人时，

sentences.en: And that's the advantage over something like green screen, where, you know, you see somebody on a green screen set,
sentences.zh: 你几乎立刻就能看出来，因为他们脸上的阴影反射着……

sentences.en: and you can tell almost immediately because the shadows on their faces are reflecting...
sentences.zh: 一切看起来都是灰蒙蒙的。

sentences.en: Everything looks gray.
sentences.zh: 那种对比度不足的感觉……

sentences.en: There's that under-contrasted, like...
sentences.zh: 而且通常如果你仔细看，你可以看到一点点绿色的痕迹，比如在面对色度背景的那一侧有背反射。

sentences.en: And typically, if you look very closely, you can see the little hint of the green, like, back reflectance on whatever side is facing the chroma backdrop.
sentences.zh: 在他们身后，而使用LED墙，你的光线就是环境的反射，这更接近现实生活。

sentences.en: Behind them, whereas with the LED wall, your light is the reflectance of whatever the environment is, which is much closer to real life.
sentences.zh: 这就是你谈到过的……

sentences.en: And that's something that, like, you've talked about in...
sentences.zh: 特别是在《治愈现代灵魂》中，直觉如何根据那些微小的感知来判断某样东西是否真实。

sentences.en: Especially in the, like, healing the modern soul, the way that intuition kind of picks up whether or not something feels real, based on those, like, micro-perceptions.
sentences.zh: 我们在思考之前，就已经知道自己是否喜欢它，或者它是否真实。

sentences.en: That we basically, before we think about it, we already know if we like it or not, or if it's real or not.
sentences.zh: 没错，就像那些微妙的东西，除非你知道去寻找，否则你不会注意到。

sentences.en: Exactly, and it's like there's those, like, subtle things that, like, you don't look for unless you know to look for them.
sentences.zh: 但作为一名设计师，你的整个世界就是试图在观众发现之前捕捉到这些东西并进行修正。

sentences.en: But as a designer, like, that's your whole world is, like, trying to pick up on those things before the audience does and correcting for them.
sentences.zh: 所以LED墙技术，能够创造这种环境。

sentences.en: So that technology of the LED wall, being able to create this environment.
sentences.zh: 另一个推论是实时图形的进步，即创造照片级或近乎照片级环境的能力，

sentences.en: And then the corollary one is the advances in real-time graphics, the ability to create photoreal or near photoreal,
sentences.zh: 你可以即时生成这些环境，并追踪物理世界中的摄像机运动，

sentences.en: real-time environments that you can generate on the fly that are tracking things like the camera movement in the physical world,
sentences.zh: 与虚拟环境中的摄像机相关联，这样当你平移摄像机扫过表演者时，LED墙中的摄像机也在移动，并随之移动你的场景。

sentences.en: correlated to a camera in the virtual environment, so that as you pan the camera across the performer, the camera in the LED wall is also moving and moving your scenery with it.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时完成这些事情，感觉比你在外景拍摄时看起来更真实，

sentences.en: And you can do those kinds of things in real-time in a way that feels much closer to how it would look if you were shooting on location somewhere,
sentences.zh: 而不是像绿幕那样，需要有人放置追踪点，并在后期制作中进行物理移动。

sentences.en: as opposed to the green screen where it's, like, someone's got to place trackers and, like, physically move in post-production.
sentences.zh: 我们现在在拍摄时就能在摄像机中捕捉到所有这些。

sentences.en: We're now capturing all of that in the camera as the shot is being done.
sentences.zh: 这在创造这些东西的速度以及你能够创造的保真度上都是一个巨大的飞跃。

sentences.en: And it's just such a huge jump in the speed at which you can create those things and also the fidelity at which you're able to create them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且在很多人不喜欢的《星球大战》前传三部曲中，

sentences.en: Well, and there's almost, like, in the prequel trilogy that a lot of people didn't like,
sentences.zh: 有一处场景几乎和后传三部曲中的一模一样，我觉得人们肯定更喜欢后传那种看起来的效果，至少是这样。

sentences.en: there's almost the exact same scene at one point as in the sequel trilogy that I think people definitely liked the way it looked, at least, you know, more.
sentences.zh: 欧比旺坐在飞船的球形驾驶舱里，必须有一个激光束经过，然后他必须对此做出反应。

sentences.en: But there's, like, Obi-Wan is in the bubble cockpit of a ship, and there has to be, like, a laser blast goes by, and then he has to react to it.
sentences.zh: 但在前传三部曲中，他们制作它的方式——这并不奏效，或者感觉有些不对劲——是剧本必须写上“对激光束做出反应”。

sentences.en: But the way that they're making it in the prequel trilogy, which doesn't really work or something feels wrong, is that the script has to say, reacts to laser blasts.
sentences.zh: 所以，伊万·麦克格雷格必须做出“哇”的表情，然后抬头看。

sentences.en: So, you know, Elon McGregor has to go, whoa, and look up.
sentences.zh: 然后动画师必须在他抬头看的同时回去制作这个激光束。

sentences.en: And then an animator has to go back in at about the same time that he looks up and make this blaSt.
sentences.zh: 但这两者之间没有真正的联系。

sentences.en: But there was no real connection between those things.
sentences.zh: 而当奥斯卡·伊萨克在另一部电影的X翼战机驾驶舱里时，你知道，他坐在屏幕前，实时感受着声音和光线。

sentences.en: And when Oscar Isaac's in the X-Wing cockpit, you know, in the other one, he's sitting there on a screen with the sound and the light in real time.
sentences.zh: 所以你看到他注意到激光束经过，击中某物，爆炸，抬头看，这种反应不是人为制造的惊喜。

sentences.en: So you see him notice the laser blast go by, hit something, explosion, look up, in a way that is not a manufactured surprise.
sentences.zh: 或者说，电影的各个部分之间有真正的联系，我认为这就是人们批评2000年代初技术的地方。

sentences.en: Or, you know, there's an actual connection between the parts of the film, which I think is, like, what people criticize about technology of, like, the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 你知道，2010年代存在这种脱节，东西是相隔数周或数月制作出来的，然后以一种并不真正奏效的方式合成在一起。

sentences.en: And, you know, 2010s was that there was this disconnect where things were being made, you know, weeks and months apart and synthesized together in a way that didn't really work.
sentences.zh: 是的，它感觉脱节，因为表演者不知道他们到底在对什么做出反应。

sentences.en: And then, yeah, and it feels disjointed because the performers don't know exactly what it is that they're reacting to.
sentences.zh: 而创作者，你知道，那些在后期制作中加入这些的技术艺术家，不得不处理这种预先录制好的反应，而你可以在现代虚拟制作环境中实时处理这些事情。

sentences.en: And the creators, you know, the technical artists that are putting that in and post are having to, like, work with this, like, pre-canned sort of reaction, whereas you can kind of,
sentences.zh: 另一个你现在能做而那个时代做不到的伟大例子，实际上是他穿的曼达洛人盔甲。

sentences.en: like, you know, work with those things in real time in more of a modern virtual production environment.
sentences.zh: 那全是那种明亮的、超级反光的铬金属。

sentences.en: Another, like, great example of, like, things that you can do now that you couldn't do in that era is actually the Mandalorian armor that he wears.
sentences.zh: 它会反射绿幕。

sentences.en: It's all that bright, like, super reflective chrome.
sentences.zh: 是的，你只能在曼达洛人的LED墙环境中才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: It'd be reflecting green screen.
sentences.zh: 但能够实现这种效果而不必去外景地或搭建复杂的布景，真是太酷了，

sentences.en: Yeah, you can only get away with that in the Mandalorian LED wall environment.
sentences.zh: 因为那也是真正令人印象深刻的事情之一。

sentences.en: But it's such a cool effect to be able to achieve without and without having to go on location or, like, build an elaborate set,
sentences.zh: 对于那部剧来说，他们实现这一切的预算，你知道，在10年前会是现在的10倍或20倍。

sentences.en: because that's one of the things that was really impressive.
sentences.zh: 那也是真正令人印象深刻的事情之一。

sentences.en: For that show was also the budget on which they were able to achieve all of that, you know, would have been 10 or, you know, 20 times as expensive 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 对于那部剧来说，他们实现这一切的预算，你知道，在10年前会是现在的10倍或20倍。

sentences.en: Well, and when you can do anything, when you're trying to run through a giant set and have a J.J.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当你能做任何事的时候，当你试图去跑完一整套庞大的布景，还要加上一段J.J. Abrams风格的20分钟开场，

sentences.en: Abrams style 20 minute introduction where they're dodging a hole in the ship while they're explaining how the world works.
sentences.zh: 他们一边躲避飞船上的破洞，一边解释这个世界是如何运作的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's something about that that is compelling, but I kind of like how the writing for the set has forced writing to go back to almost like plays, you know?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这其中确实有某种引人入胜的东西，但我其实挺喜欢这种布景创作迫使写作回归到几乎像戏剧一样的形式，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're having Yoda talk to Luke in the swamp for a long time, whereas there's no scene like that in the prequel trilogy.
sentences.zh: 你让尤达大师在沼泽里和卢克谈了很久，而前传三部曲里根本没有那样的场景。

sentences.en: It's always just a huge whirlwind of a million things.
sentences.zh: 那里面永远是一团乱麻，充斥着数不清的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's, you know, it's, to dust off my theater history for a second, it's a little bit like the difference between the desire for, like, unity of place versus the, like,
sentences.zh: 是啊，你知道，为了稍微掸掉我戏剧史上的灰尘，这有点像是在追求“地点统一”与那种……

sentences.en: sweeping opera kind of, like, set design where you'd have, like, backdrop after backdrop that they would just fly in.
sentences.zh: 宏大的歌剧式舞台设计之间的区别，那种你会不断更换背景，直接吊装上来的设计。

sentences.en: And these really elaborately painted, like, massive scenic pieces versus, like, having an entire play, basically, that takes place in one location over one, like,
sentences.zh: 还有那些制作极其精良、巨大的风景片，与之相对的，是基本上整部戏都在一个地点，在一段……

sentences.en: contiguous span of time.
sentences.zh: 连续的时间跨度内完成。

sentences.en: And those are just different philosophies that have fallen in and out of fashion over the years.
sentences.zh: 这些只是多年来时兴时衰的不同哲学理念。

sentences.en: But it's like, we're in another cycle of that right now as we, as we,
sentences.zh: 但现在我们又处于另一个周期中，随着我们……

sentences.en: as the technology available drives some of the creative of the story that you want to tell and how you want to tell it.
sentences.zh: 随着可用的技术驱动了你想要讲述的故事的创意，以及你想要讲述它的方式。

sentences.en: And I don't like to say it that way, right?
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢这么说，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, the tech should never be the tail wagging the dog of the story.
sentences.zh: 技术永远不应该成为牵着故事鼻子走的那条尾巴。

sentences.en: But sometimes in exploration, you find opportunities to tell a better story with the tools that you have available to you.
sentences.zh: 但有时在探索中，你会发现利用现有的工具去讲一个更好的故事的机会。

sentences.en: Well, and that's my question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我的问题所在。

sentences.en: It's like, a lot of people, if you say that you're in tech, in theater, you know, movies, they hear technology and they think of Sam Altman saying,
sentences.zh: 很多人，如果你说你在科技、戏剧、电影行业工作，他们一听到技术，就会想到萨姆·奥特曼说：

sentences.en: well, we're not even going to have actors anymore.
sentences.zh: “好吧，我们甚至不再需要演员了。”

sentences.en: We're just, you know, going to have generated video through generative AI, you know, or they think of the endless blue screen.
sentences.zh: “我们只需要通过生成式AI来生成视频。”或者他们会想到无尽的蓝幕。

sentences.en: You know, they think of the, like, you know, just unending litany of effects in the Hobbit movie where there's, like, no soul, but it just goes on and on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们会想到《霍比特人》电影里那种没完没了的特效，毫无灵魂，却没完没了。

sentences.en: And they think, okay, tech is bad, which, I mean, technology, I think, in movies is inevitable.
sentences.zh: 于是他们觉得，技术是坏的。但我觉得，技术在电影中是不可避免的。

sentences.en: It's how is it used?
sentences.zh: 关键在于如何使用它？

sentences.en: I mean, can you speak to that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Or what do you say that somebody has a negative reaction to?
sentences.zh: 或者对于那些有负面反应的人，你会怎么说？

sentences.en: So I'm always very, I probably have one of the more neutral opinions on, like, AI and its current incarnation relative to a lot of people out there in so far as, like,
sentences.zh: 我一直非常……相对于很多人来说，我对AI及其当前形态的看法可能是最中立的之一，因为……

sentences.en: my experience with it has been that it's another tool in the toolkit for a lot of, like, creatives to use if they want to.
sentences.zh: 我的经验是，对于许多想要使用它的创作者来说，它是工具箱里的又一个工具。

sentences.en: Especially as it is right now, because it's not perfect, and it doesn't, in my opinion, and maybe never will be able to create stylistically the same way that a human does,
sentences.zh: 特别是在它目前的阶段，因为它并不完美，在我看来，也许永远无法像人类那样进行风格化创作，

sentences.en: you know, because it is all sort of, like, trained on what we do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为它本质上是基于我们所做的事情进行训练的。

sentences.en: It's trained on the paSt.
sentences.zh: 它是基于过去进行训练的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it'll never be able to intuit the future, at least in this current incarnation, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它永远无法直觉地预知未来，至少在目前的形态下是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, there's a world 10, 20 years from now where maybe it does that, and I can't possibly know.
sentences.zh: 也许10年、20年后会有那样的世界，但我无法预知。

sentences.en: But right now, I think something that it's interesting with, and this is actually something I'm interested to hear your take on, is that, like, because it's trained on the past,
sentences.zh: 但现在，我觉得它有趣的地方在于——这也是我很想听听你看法的地方——因为它基于过去进行训练，

sentences.en: because it's trained on this sort of, like, imprint of so much raw data that has been input by humanity since the dawn of the internet.
sentences.zh: 因为它基于自互联网诞生以来人类输入的大量原始数据的印记进行训练。

sentences.en: It's like, does it kind of allow us to tap into our collective unconscious, to borrow a term from Jung, and show us things that maybe we wouldn't have arrived at, you know,
sentences.zh: 这是否让我们能够借用荣格的一个术语，触及我们的集体潜意识，并向我们展示一些我们可能无法通过……

sentences.en: from our own sort of iteration and development of an idea, right?
sentences.zh: 我们自己对一个想法的迭代和发展而得出的东西呢？

sentences.en: I can go type in something I've thought about to a program like MidJourney or ChatGBT and say, draw me a picture of what this might look like.
sentences.zh: 我可以把我思考过的事情输入到像MidJourney或ChatGPT这样的程序中，说：给我画一张这看起来可能是什么样的图。

sentences.en: And it might give me a dozen results that I never would have considered, other than, like, asking the AI to, like, sling some things at me.
sentences.zh: 它可能会给我十几个我从未考虑过的结果，而不是仅仅让AI给我抛出一些东西。

sentences.en: If my tunnel vision of my perception was only going down this one specific path,
sentences.zh: 如果我感知上的隧道视野只沿着这一条特定的路径走，

sentences.en: now I've got an array of other ideas that I can at least consider and react to as a designer and say, does it speak to my vision, or is this totally off base?
sentences.zh: 现在我拥有了一系列其他的想法，作为设计师，我至少可以考虑并做出反应，看看它是否符合我的愿景，还是完全离题了？

sentences.en: And either of those responses is very useful for the, like, creative process.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种反应，对于创作过程来说都非常有用。

sentences.en: Well, I think that's it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想就是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that, like, its ability to create something like a Pinterest board, or to give you eight designs for a set, and then let you pick the one that you were wanting,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它能够像创建Pinterest看板一样，或者给你八种布景设计，然后让你挑选你想要的那一种，

sentences.en: you know, to brainstorm is probably good.
sentences.zh: 你知道，用来头脑风暴可能是不错的。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, your dreams are trained on the past, right?
sentences.zh: 因为，你的梦也是基于过去训练的，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, Jung talks about how dream is something, it's a way of thinking about the past that lets us anticipate the future based on what's happened before.
sentences.zh: 荣格谈到梦是一种思考过去的方式，让我们根据过去发生的事情来预测未来。

sentences.en: So, you know, like, a lot of times, like, AI is, you know, especially the visual stuff, it is dreaming, it's, like, free associating with patterns,
sentences.zh: 所以，很多时候，AI，特别是视觉方面，它是在做梦，它是在对模式进行自由联想，

sentences.en: which is what makes some of its weirdness, that it has, like, an over, because there's so many pictures of dogs on the internet, some of the early versions were, like,
sentences.zh: 这正是它产生一些怪异感的原因，因为互联网上有太多的狗的照片，一些早期版本被……

sentences.en: overtrained to spot faces of dogs.
sentences.zh: 过度训练以识别狗的脸。

sentences.en: So, they would, like, put dog faces inside of, like, you know, beard pattern, or just places where it might see a pattern.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们会把狗脸放在胡须图案里，或者任何它可能看到图案的地方。

sentences.en: So, I mean, to me, that's so interesting, because you're getting into the stuff that I think is neat about, you know, psychosis, and, you know, the kind of deep brain,
sentences.zh: 所以，对我来说，这太有趣了，因为你触及到了我认为关于精神病和深层大脑的有趣之处，

sentences.en: but to put a pin on that as a short point, like, I think that a lot of the newer brain science that is interesting to me,
sentences.zh: 但简单总结一下，我认为很多我感兴趣的较新的脑科学研究，

sentences.en: and clarifies things that never understood about the old pattern, is that there's so much, it's, the brain isn't really processing, like,
sentences.zh: 澄清了以前对旧模式不理解的地方，那就是大脑并不是真的在处理……

sentences.en: that's not really the key to understanding cognition, there's so much processing happening, so are all the time.
sentences.zh: 那并不是理解认知的关键，大脑一直在进行大量的处理。

sentences.en: Consciousness is more of a filter.
sentences.zh: 意识更多是一种过滤器。

sentences.en: It's more of, what am I ignoring to focus on this, you know?
sentences.zh: 更多是关于：为了专注于这一点，我忽略了什么，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that, things like the sensory gating theory of schizophrenia, a lot of these newer theories are saying, like, well, when these problems with cognition happen,
sentences.zh: 像精神分裂症的感觉门控理论，许多这些较新的理论都在说，当这些认知问题发生时，

sentences.en: it's not that something is being created that didn't used to be there, it's that there's something not being filtered out that should be.
sentences.zh: 并不是创造出了以前不存在的东西，而是有些本该被过滤掉的东西没有被过滤掉。

sentences.en: And so, those AIs are essentially filters, they're going through a ton of what has been done by somebody else before, which makes it inherently not original, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以，这些AI本质上就是过滤器，它们在筛选别人以前做过的大量东西，这使得它本质上并不原创，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then they're looking at, how can we combine these in a way that reflects what you're asking me to do, which is a great way to brainstorm.
sentences.zh: 然后它们在研究如何以一种反映你要求我做的方式来组合这些东西，这是一种很好的头脑风暴方式。

sentences.en: Doug Reshkoff said that, you know, he wrote these novels, and then he improved the novels, because he asked an AI, hey, what does a character do in all of these situations?
sentences.zh: 道格·拉什科夫说过，他写了这些小说，然后他改进了这些小说，因为他问AI：嘿，角色在所有这些情况下会做什么？

sentences.en: And everywhere where it said to do what he had done, he said, that's not a good, that's not, that's not good, like, and that it ended up, he,
sentences.zh: 凡是AI建议做他已经做过的事情的地方，他就说：那不好，那不好，那不好。结果他……

sentences.en: but he never would have spotted those 30% of the tropes that were kind of lazy in his writing if it wasn't a computer saying, well, why don't they do this?
sentences.zh: 但他永远不会发现他写作中那30%比较懒惰的套路，如果不是电脑说：嗯，他们为什么不这样做呢？

sentences.en: And that's what he had come up with.
sentences.zh: 而那正是他想出来的。

sentences.en: So, I think, like, that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我觉得，像那样。

sentences.en: Also, so much of filmmaking is, like, juxtaposing weird genres, you know?
sentences.zh: 而且，电影制作中很大一部分是把奇怪的类型并置在一起，你懂吗？

sentences.en: Like, a lot of the really influential stuff is, like, getting two really weird ideas and then putting them together to make a new thing, a space western or something.
sentences.zh: 很多非常有影响力的作品，就是把两个非常奇怪的想法放在一起，创造出一个新东西，比如太空西部片之类的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I could see it being helpful for something like that, because you've got, it knows what this is, it knows what that is, you combine it,
sentences.zh: 我能看出它对这类事情很有帮助，因为它知道这是什么，那是什么，你把它们结合起来，

sentences.en: and then it's giving you interesting ideas about how to make a set, or how to do something like that, maybe.
sentences.zh: 然后它会给你关于如何制作布景，或者如何做类似事情的有趣想法，也许吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, something I've found that it's really good at is that kind of, like, stylistic transposition, you know, where it's like you have, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，我发现它非常擅长那种风格转换，你知道，就是你把……

sentences.en: something that you feed into it, an image of some kind, and you say, show me this in these different, like, styles, right?
sentences.zh: 你输入给它的某种图像，然后说：用这些不同的风格展示给我看，对吧？

sentences.en: Or show me this in Star Wars, you know, or Transformers or Ghostbusters or, like, whatever the paradigm may be.
sentences.zh: 或者在《星球大战》、《变形金刚》、《捉鬼敢死队》或者任何范式中展示给我看。

sentences.en: But it's like, because it knows all of those things, it knows all the pop culture references, it can do this sort of interesting, you know, there's a real bunny hole there.
sentences.zh: 但因为它知道所有这些东西，它知道所有的流行文化参考，它可以做这种有趣的……这里面确实有个兔子洞。

sentences.en: But, like, you can modulate a bunch of settings and then get a certain amount of, like, your input versus the AI, you know, kind of a trace over of your given, like,
sentences.zh: 但是，你可以调节一堆设置，然后获得一定程度的你的输入与AI的结合，你知道，有点像是在你的图像或想法上进行描摹。

sentences.en: image or thought.
sentences.zh: 然后让它吐出一些……嗯，这看起来可能是这样的，你懂吗？

sentences.en: And then have it, like, spit back out some, like, well, this is what it could look like, you know?
sentences.zh: 嗯，对于视觉特效，我觉得它可以是一个很好的润色工具，当你得到了你想要的特效的大致轮廓时，

sentences.en: Well, and for, like, VFX, I could see it being a good polisher, that when you get the broad strokes of the effect that you're going for,
sentences.zh: 它进去清理光线，或者清理水的熔融特性，或者魔法咒语反射的光线。

sentences.en: it goes in and it cleans up the light rays, or it cleans up the molten property of the water or the magic spell reflecting, you know, light around.
sentences.zh: 它不需要一百名工程师团队去逐一进行视觉修改。

sentences.en: It doesn't require, you know, a team of 100 engineers to go through and visually change each thing.
sentences.zh: 但你仍然需要拥有愿景的人类元素，我认为这是AI做不到的。

sentences.en: But you still would need the human element of having the vision, which I think AI can't do.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 它无法区分自己的噪音，你懂吗？

sentences.en: It can't distinguish between its own noise, you know?
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我绝对认为，在它目前的阶段，我绝不会考虑在没有人类干预的情况下将其用于完全成品。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I, definitely where it is now, it's not something that I would ever consider as, like, using for a totally finished product with no human intervention.
sentences.zh: 它还没到那个程度，但所有这些技术以某种方式融合在一起，对我来说非常有趣。

sentences.en: It's like, it's not, it's definitely not there yet, but it's just very interesting to me, the way that all of these technologies have kind of, like, come together.
sentences.zh: 它们都是基于相同的电路，你懂吗？

sentences.en: It's all sort of based on the same circuitry, you know?
sentences.zh: 用于摄像机内视觉特效的实时图形是基于GPU的，对吧？

sentences.en: The real-time graphics for in-camera VFX, that is GPU-based, right?
sentences.zh: 所有的AI技术也是如此。

sentences.en: And then so is all of the AI stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以这些能够进行快速计算的特定高性能电路，正是推动我们如何为娱乐业大规模快速创作的时刻的动力。

sentences.en: And so these very specific high-powered circuits that can do all this fast compute are the things that are driving kind of the moment of how we approach creating things rapidly at scale for entertainment.
sentences.zh: 这在电影和演唱会制作中都是如此，你知道，演唱会有时是电影的缩影，因为你正在为摄像机拍摄这种……

sentences.en: And that's true across, like, film and across concert production, which, you know, sometimes is sort of a microcosm of film because you're shooting this, like,
sentences.zh: 现场体验。

sentences.en: live experience for camera.
sentences.zh: 但过去20年里发生的每一场演出，艺人身后都有一个巨大的LED墙。

sentences.en: But every show that's happened in the last 20 years has had a big LED wall behind the talent anyways.
sentences.zh: 你也在拍摄那个，在某种程度上它成了你的背景。
